text:
Alex: Heads-up on bring-up: rk-v3-int4 shows weird offline/online split. Offline eval: NDCG +3.0% but MRR -4.2%. Canary CTR dropped ~2.5% after dedupe+prune change. Anyone seen int4 interact badly with dedupe?
Marisol: Can you paste the exact eval flags and candidate pipeline config? 
Alex: Eval command: ```./eval_rerank --model rk-v3-int4 --anchors handset_v4 --candidates 200 --seed 7 --metrics ndcg,mrr``` Pipeline had `prune.topk=50` and `dedupe.threshold=0.85` (min_sim dedupe). We applied per-channel int4 quant w/ symmetric scale.
Toby: Quick thought: dedupe removes near-duplicates; int4 might compress embedding geometry so distances cluster -> more removals. That would reduce MRR if the best answer was dropped but NDCG (which averages over positions) can still look fine.
Lina: Also check unicode normalization + tokenization parity. Our near-dup detector normalizes whitespace+nfkc, but the new tokenizer binary used in canary skipped nfkc in one build earlier.
Marisol: I ran a small ablation on sampled_prod_holdout: dedupe=off -> MRR recovers. Numbers: dedupe ON: NDCG +2.9% / MRR -3.8% vs baseline. dedupe OFF: NDCG +1.7% / MRR +0.9% vs baseline. So dedupe seems to be the culprit in combination.
DeployBot: Canary 2026-03-23T15:10:00Z deployed rk-v3-int4 to canary-2 (10% traffic). Canary policy: auto-rollback on CTR <= -2% over 1h.
Alex: Good catch. My hypothesis: int4 embedding quant reduces cosine dynamic range -> pairs that used to be <0.85 similarity now look >0.85 and get deduped. Need to verify embed norm/rescale after quantization.
Toby: Suggest running pairwise distance histogram pre/post quant for a 5k sample and sweep dedupe threshold 0.7->0.95. Quick snippet I use: ```python
emb_fp = load_embeddings('fp16')
emb_q = load_embeddings('int4')
dists_fp = cosine_pairwise(emb_fp[:5000])
dists_q = cosine_pairwise(emb_q[:5000])
plot_hist(dists_fp, dists_q)
```
Lina: I'm spinning that probe now and will also check tokenizer checksums and normalization flags. Also will log a few concrete query examples where top candidate got removed.
Marisol: Opening issue tracker entry #2042: "dedupe vs quantized-embeddings regression" with links to eval jobs + sample candidates. Adding triage label and assigning to Alex/Toby/Lina. Also adding onboarding checklist item: for any quantized ranker bring-up, run dedupe-sensitivity sweep and embedding-distance histograms.
Alex: Can we also add a temporary mitigation: lower dedupe threshold to 0.8 in canary config and observe CTR? If that recovers, we can keep it while we investigate proper calibration.
DeployBot: Canary config update requested. Lowered dedupe.threshold to 0.8 for rk-v3-int4 canary-2. New health monitor engaged.
Toby: I'll work on a small per-channel embedding re-scale after quant (post-quant calibrate) to restore pairwise separation. Prototype code: ```python
scales = compute_pcq_scales(emb_fp, emb_q)
emb_q_rescaled = emb_q * scales
```
Lina: Probe results incoming in ~20m. I'll include histograms and 10 example query->candidate traces.
Alex: Thanks team. If histograms show compression, we'll add post-quant rescale to the quant pipeline and update the bring-up doc. Also collecting anonymized candidate examples for manual review (5 per affected query).
Marisol: Noted. Tracking PRs and issues in the ticket. Will follow-up with a short writeup for the onboarding doc once we confirm repro. :thumbsup:
